222e66a510036328:5908.summary: A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's networking code, tracked as CVE-2026-99999 and nicknamed PwnEscape, allows code running inside a guest virtual machine to read host memory, crash the host, or execute code. Discovered by security researcher Paulos Yibelo, the flaw was successfully demonstrated against production sandboxes at Vercel, allowing a guest to exfiltrate 32 bytes of host memory per packet. The vulnerability resides in the shared kernel networking layer utilized by cloud providers for workload isolation, rather than in specific cloud configurations or hypervisors like Firecracker. Assigned a CVSS severity score of 9.3, the local attack vector requires initial code execution within a guest environment.
222e66a510036328:5908.one_liner: A critical Linux kernel networking flaw named PwnEscape lets guest virtual machines read host memory and break out of isolation layers.
222e66a510036328:5908.bottom_line: Shared kernel networking layers in cloud environments can harbor cross-boundary memory leakage flaws that compromise multi-tenant workload isolation.

a9f64dded404b64f:3838.summary: LovelyCarve is an open-source, read-only desktop and CLI disk forensics and data recovery utility built with Rust, Tauri 2, and Vue 3. It provides comprehensive evidence ingestion supporting physical disks, logical images, AD1, Docker/OCI images, iOS backups, and RAID reconstructions alongside decrypted views for BitLocker, LUKS, VeraCrypt, and FileVault 2. 3a7b569916d74508:11471.summary: Project Zero researchers detailed a privilege escalation vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-66804, an incomplete fix for the Dark Elevator bug (CVE-2026-50343) in Windows. The root cause stems from a dangling system-wide COM object registration for the CrossDevice component pointing to a missing DLL path inside the unprotected C:\ProgramData directory. Because normal users can create directories within ProgramData, an attacker can plant an arbitrary DLL. By sending a custom COM marshaling structure specifying the dangling CLSID to a privileged service, the runtime automatically loads the arbitrary DLL and achieves privilege escalation.
3a7b569916d74508:11471.one_liner: A dangling COM object registration combined with custom COM marshaling enables privilege escalation on Windows via planted DLLs.
3a7b569916d74508:11471.bottom_line: CVE-2026-66804 allows unprivileged users to achieve local privilege escalation by exploiting a dangling COM object registration and custom COM marshaling.

2c47c452245d7d72:13795.summary: The US synthetic opioid crisis has deepened with the proliferation of cheap, homemade drug mixtures cut with powerful animal tranquilizers like Xylazine and Medetomidine. Fentanyl and its synthetic analogs are now frequently adulterated with these sedatives, which slow breathing, cause severe necrotic skin ulcers, and crucially resist reversal via standard Naloxone (Narcan) administration. dc8cec88b45e7cd3:21741.summary: Earshot is an open-source, CPU-local tool designed to give AI coding agents the ability to hear, review, and synthesize audio code. ed4de16917e5b3e3:20300.summary: Unit 42 investigated a September 2024 multi-stage intrusion (CL-STA-0954) against a telecom provider, initiated by exploiting CVE-2024-47575 on a FortiManager appliance. The attackers exfiltrated configuration and credential archives for over 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, and subsequently exploited CVE-2025-61624 via path traversal to deploy PEERSTITCH, a stealthy memory-resident ARM64 malware that leaves no disk artifacts and blends with legitimate traffic.
ed4de16917e5b3e3:20300.one_liner: Attackers exploited FortiManager and FortiOS vulnerabilities to exfiltrate firewall configs and deploy the memory-resident PEERSTITCH malware.
ed4de16917e5b3e3:20300.bottom_line: Nation-state tradecraft involving Fortinet appliance vulnerabilities allows attackers to silently manage firewall infrastructure via memory-resident malware.

claims.text: The exploit of CVE-2025-61624 facilitated the deployment of PEERSTITCH, a novel memory-resident ARM64 malware.
claims.support_span: The attackers exploited another vulnerability, CVE-2025-61624, via FortiOS auto-script path traversal. This exploit facilitated the deployment of PEERSTITCH, a novel, memory-resident ARM64 malware.

6f9b0a9070ef1a3e:8955.summary: Cisco Talos and Recorded Future identified a threat cluster tracked as UAT-6275 (or TAG-193) targeting government, water, and energy organizations across Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) countries. Operating from June 2025 to August 2026, the group used macro-enabled documents, PS2EXE downloaders, GitHub-hosted scripts, and a WinRAR archive exploit (CVE-2025-8088) to deliver custom reverse shells. Operational security failures, including exposed staging directories and GitHub repositories, exposed their tooling and infrastructure.
6f9b0a9070ef1a3e:8955.one_liner: UAT-6275 targeted CIS government and critical infrastructure with custom reverse shells and exploits, exposing operations via insecure staging directories.
6f9b0a9070ef1a3e:8955.bottom_line: State-nexus actors targeting CIS government and infrastructure can be tracked via opsec lapses like exposed staging directories and GitHub repos.

claims.text: Cisco Talos identified UAT-6275 targeting government organizations across the Commonwealth of Independent States.
claims.support_span: - Cisco Talos identified UAT-6275 (TAG-193 by Recorded Future) activity targeting government organizations across the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).

claims.text: Three publicly accessible staging directories and GitHub repository history exposed payload builds and tool inventories.

00b001f454de8f6c:31973.summary: A technical analysis details the construction of a full Android kernel exploit chain on a Pixel 6 running Android 12 (kernel 5.10) using CVE-2023-20938, a use-after-free vulnerability in the Binder IPC driver. claims.support_span: We run it on a Pixel 6 with Android 12 and kernel 5.10 (arm64).
